task_name: Redecker Machine Works - Restored mark system
client_brief:
Restore a machineworks identity from a catalogue and an etched plate

Redecker's mark has a long history, but the source artwork has not survived. We have a 1974 catalogue and an etched plate to work from. We want the identity recovered carefully, not replaced with something that merely looks industrial.

The commission

 Engineering identity master: 1 named export. The mark preserves the surviving original identity. Letter counters remain open at the smallest size the mark is reproduced on the machine plate or the service header.

 Machine identity plate: 1 named export. The plate carries the company mark and the REDECKER plate wordmark, and its information matches the supplied machine record for the special build. The production lettering is legible, and the plate field labels follow the type system scale: Suisse Int'l Regular 400 at 7 pt, tracked 0.080 em.

 Service document header: 1 named export. The company name is correct, and the header carries the company mark, the REDECKER wordmark and the works address block. The header sits at the top of the page and leaves the page below it clear for service content.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Manufacturer of press brakes and metal forming presses, capital equipment sold to procurement engineers and plant managers across North America and northern Europe
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1919 in Sheboygan, Wisconsin; third generation family works, forty one people
brand_identity.about: Redecker builds press brakes and metal forming presses, from forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars a machine. The works has carried the same company mark since 1919. Our buyer reads the tolerance sheet before he reads anything we wrote, so everything we put a name on has to say precision.
brand_identity.audience: Procurement engineers and plant managers who buy on specification rather than feeling, across North America and northern Europe
brand_identity.price_positioning: Capital equipment at forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars per machine. The mark is read as evidence about the machine: the register is flat, mechanical, high contrast and generously spaced, never heritage craft workshop and never consumer tech.

palette.name: Works Green
palette.role: mandatory on the machine plate, as its field, and in works-mark.svg, as the colour of the full-colour master; optional on the service header
palette.usage: The solid field of the machine plate and the ground the mark and all plate wording reverse out of (redecker_works_standards.txt: the FIELD colour, HEX 33564A as the paint shop mixes it). The colour of the mark, and of any wordmark set with it, in works-mark.svg (redecker_works_standards.txt variant 1, "Master (full colour)"). On the service header, optional: a ground, or on a light ground a colour for the mark, the wordmark or type.

palette.name: Machine Black
palette.usage: The one-colour version of the mark (redecker_works_standards.txt: the one-colour stamp, variant 2, "One-colour (Machine Black) for the invoice stamp"), and type or the mark on a Signal White or Cream Board ground of the service header. Never in works-mark.svg, the full-colour master; never on Works Green; never a ground.

palette.name: Plate Steel
palette.role: mandatory where the REDECKER wordmark is set
palette.usage: The 0.5 pt rule directly beneath the REDECKER wordmark at exactly its width, and hairline rules outside the mark, such as the rule above the plate's works address block. Never type, never the mark or its rings, never a panel or a ground.

palette.name: Cream Board
palette.usage: An optional paper ground for the service header, the board of redecker_catalogue_1974_cover.tif. Never type, never the mark, never on the machine plate or in works-mark.svg.

palette.name: Signal White
palette.role: mandatory where type or the mark sits on Works Green
palette.usage: All plate wording and the reversed mark on Works Green (redecker_works_standards.txt: reversed wording on plates), hairline rules on Works Green, and an optional paper ground for the service header, where unprinted paper counts as Signal White. Never the colour of the mark in works-mark.svg.

brand_identity.typography: Redecker Machine Works runs on Sohne Breit Halbfett for display and Suisse Int'l for text, with Suisse Int'l Mono held back for serials. Step 01, display, is Sohne Breit Halbfett capitals at 14 pt on 15 pt leading tracked 0.200 em, the plate wordmark, with a 0.5 pt Plate Steel rule directly beneath it at exactly the wordmark width; the same setting runs at 32 px on 40 px on screen with the tracking unchanged. Step 02, subheading, is the same face in capitals at 7 pt on 9 pt leading on the same 0.200 em tracking, which is exactly half the cap height of step 01 and carries MACHINE WORKS below the rule; plate field labels also sit at 7 pt but in Suisse Int'l Regular 400 tracked 0.080 em. Step 03, body, is Suisse Int'l Regular 400 at 9.5 pt on 13 pt leading, tracking zero, set to a maximum of 65 characters for A4 stationery and specification sheets. Step 04, fine print, is Suisse Int'l Mono Regular 400 at 7 pt on 10 pt leading tracked 0.040 em for serials and plate labels, with the value itself at 9 pt on the same 10 pt leading directly under its label. The mark is never condensed and never italicised.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, factual and confident; we state the specification and let it stand. No adjectives a tolerance sheet would not carry. Example line the brand would write: "Built to a hundred years of the same standard, plate by plate."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We no longer hold usable artwork for the company mark in any form. The designer who last touched it retired in the nineties and nothing came back from his files. What survives is a flatbed scan of the 1974 parts catalogue cover, where the mark is printed in one deep ink on cream board, and a photograph a fitter took of the same mark etched into a stainless nameplate on a machine that came back for a rebuild. A works standards text file records the green as the paint shop mixes it, the address block and the required plate wording. Two further company marks also survive only as artefacts: the works proving stamp, held only as a die impression struck into a steel test coupon a fitter photographed, and the 1919 cast heritage device, held only as a raking light photograph of the badge cast and painted into a machine's main frame.
brand_identity.values: Precision as reputation: the mark on a two hundred thousand dollar machine has to be as true as the machine, reversed clean out of the works green, and unmistakably ours.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: REDECKER is always set in caps tracked open to 0.20 em with a 0.5 pt Plate Steel rule directly beneath it at exactly the wordmark width, so the gaps between letters read before the letterforms do.

type_system.text_face: Suisse Int'l Regular 400 (Suisse Int'l Mono Regular 400 for serials)

scale.note: The company mark at nameplate size. A 0.5 pt Plate Steel rule sits directly beneath it at exactly the wordmark width. On screen the same setting runs at 32 px on 40 px, tracking unchanged. The gaps are the mark: they are never closed to fit a space.

scale.role: Subheading / H2 · works line and field labels
scale.note: Set at exactly half the cap height of step 01, on the same 0.200 em tracking, directly below the rule. Plate field labels also set at 7 pt, but in Suisse Int'l Regular 400 tracked 0.080 em, so a label is never mistaken for the mark.

scale.sample: Built to a hundred years of the same standard, plate by plate.
scale.note: A4 stationery, quotations and specification sheets. No adjective a tolerance sheet would not carry.

scale.role: Fine print · serials and plate values
scale.sample: REDECKER MACHINE WORKS · SHEBOYGAN, WISCONSIN · SINCE 1919
scale.note: Serial numbers, capacities and tolerances. The value itself sets at 9 pt on the same 10 pt leading directly under its 7 pt label, so figures align down the plate.

type_system.signature_move: REDECKER is always set in capitals tracked open to 0.200 em with a 0.5 pt Plate Steel rule directly beneath it at exactly the wordmark width, and MACHINE WORKS below at half the cap height on the same tracking, so the gaps between the letters read before the letterforms do.
rules: REDECKER always sets in capitals at exactly 0.200 em tracking; the tracking is never reduced to fit a space.
The rule beneath the wordmark is always 0.5 pt Plate Steel at exactly the wordmark width, no wider and no narrower.
MACHINE WORKS always sits below at half the cap height of the wordmark, on the same 0.200 em tracking.
Suisse Int'l Regular 400 sets stationery; Suisse Int'l Mono Regular 400 sets serials and nothing else sets them.
The register stays flat, mechanical, high contrast and generously spaced: never heritage craft workshop, never consumer tech.
No adjective a tolerance sheet would not carry.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds are Works Green, Signal White or Cream Board and nothing else: the machine plate's field is Works Green, with no band or panel of any other colour on the plate; works-mark.svg has a transparent ground; on the service header, unprinted paper counts as the Signal White ground. In works-mark.svg, the full-colour master (variant 1, "Master (full colour)" in redecker_works_standards.txt), the mark and any wordmark set with it are Works Green; Machine Black is the one-colour stamp of variant 2, "One-colour (Machine Black) for the invoice stamp", not this file; Plate Steel appears there only as the 0.5 pt rule beneath a REDECKER wordmark; Cream Board and Signal White never. On Works Green, all type and the mark are Signal White, and the only other colour there is a Plate Steel or Signal White rule. On Signal White or Cream Board, type and the mark are Machine Black or Works Green. Works Green is not required on the service header. Plate Steel is used only for the 0.5 pt rule beneath the REDECKER wordmark and hairline rules outside the mark, never for type, the mark or a ground.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, pattern, shadow, filter or blend mode is applied to any palette colour on the machine plate, the service header or in works-mark.svg, and no scrim or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over anything.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, grounds, rules, the mark or icons. No metallic, brushed-steel, chrome, gold or silver effect, and no texture, distressing, halftone dot, bevel, emboss or drop shadow: the register is flat, mechanical and high contrast, never heritage craft workshop and never consumer tech.
palette_rules.photography: The supplied photographs and the catalogue scan are recovery sources, not artwork: none is placed in a deliverable as the mark or in its place, and no palette colour is sampled from them. Works Green is HEX 33564A as the paint shop mixes it, not the painted casting in redecker_frame_casting_1919.jpg, and Cream Board is HEX E8E2D2, not the aged board of redecker_catalogue_1974_cover.tif.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
